extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Metamath Proof Assistant; mathematicians and students learning to construct formal Metamath proofs and to edit the set.mm database
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for creating, improving, saving, verifying, and editing Metamath proofs and for the logical/set-theoretic axioms used in the Metamath set.mm database. Includes operational advice for the Proof Assistant and rationale/representation of logic and set theory axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change order of mandatory hypotheses when editing
rubrics_metrics.description: If your source file contains proofs, you may not change the order of the mandatory hypotheses of any statement referenced in a later proof (e.g., swapping major and minor premises of modus ponens will break proofs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The show statement command will show you the mandatory hypotheses of a statement and their order. Violating this rule will make existing proofs incorrect and you can lose a lot of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compressed proofs also depend on mandatory hypothesis order
rubrics_metrics.description: If a statement has a compressed proof, you must not change the order of its mandatory hypotheses because the compressed proof format uses that order as part of the compression technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that swapping the names of two variables in a theorem will change the order of its mandatory hypotheses. A compressed proof can be converted to a normal one and vice-versa, but the mandatory-hypotheses order must be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodically verify proofs to ensure integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a good idea to periodically verify all proofs with 'verify proof *' to ensure their integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do this after edits to detect broken proofs early and avoid losing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safest process to edit a statement with existing dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: The safest way to edit a statement (say mytheorem) is to duplicate it, rename the original to mytheoremOLD throughout the database, re-prove the edited version, and then update statements referencing mytheoremOLD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After re-proving the edited version, update references in the Proof Assistant using 'minimize_with mytheorem /allow_growth'. This avoids invalidating dependent proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use minimize_with */brief to shorten proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proof Assistant's 'minimize_with */brief' command tries to shorten the proof and can make the process more efficient by letting you write a somewhat 'sloppy' proof and then clean up details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It cannot perform major restructurings of the overall proof, but is useful for optimizing and removing redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: improve command limitations and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The improve command can occasionally be useful for filling in essential steps, but it only tries to make use of statements that introduce no new variables in their hypotheses and will not try to improve steps containing temporary variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It will not attempt to fill in steps that require modus ponens (mp) because those introduce new-variable hypotheses; use it primarily for steps that don't introduce new variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empty substitution setting and ambiguous unification behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'empty_substitution' setting controls whether empty expressions can be substituted for variables. When the program determines there is not enough information to make an unambiguous unification choice, it will present possible unification choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turning empty_substitution off avoids some ambiguous unifications but can make the Assistant too restrictive. Usually the correct unification choice is obvious by inspection and tends to be the first one presented; incorrect choices tend to be meaningless fragments of wffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to undo assignments in the Proof Assistant
rubrics_metrics.description: When you assign steps (e.g., 'assign 3 a2'), to undo the assignment delete the corresponding step and then INITIALIZE and UNIFY if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assistant prints explicit undo instructions such as 'To undo the assignment, DELETE STEP N and INITIALIZE, UNIFY if needed.' Follow these to revert assignments safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save proofs after improvement and verify
rubrics_metrics.description: After improving a proof ('improve all' or similar), save the proof using SAVE (or 'save new_proof') and verify it with 'VERIFY PROOF'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assistant will report when it found proofs for steps and renumbered them; after that you should save the proof to the database and verify to ensure no $d violations or other issues remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof output formats and clipping for database insertion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proof Assistant can show a proof in 'normal' (readable, clip-and-insert) or 'compressed' (storage-saving) formats. 'show new_proof/normal' prints a clip-out region suitable for manual insertion into the database source file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compressed proofs are for storage reduction; you don't need to understand the encoding to recognize them. A compressed proof can always be converted to a normal one and vice-versa; show commands work equally well on both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct variable restriction ($d) to manage substitution issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Metamath uses a statement type called 'disjoint variable restriction' ($d) to express that two variables must be distinct or that a variable must not occur in a wff (e.g., '$d x y' or '$d x ϕ').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism replaces primitive notions of 'proper substitution' and 'free variable' in the Metamath axioms, making substitution rules easier to handle mechanically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid primitive 'free variable'/'proper substitution' in Metamath axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Metamath axioms for predicate calculus adopt Tarski's system S2 and eliminate textbook primitive concepts of 'free variable' and 'proper substitution' by embedding their complexity into axioms and using direct substitution plus distinct-variable provisos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This design choice produces more axioms but makes the system easier for a computer and beginners to work with; proper-substitution rules are developed later as derived constructs, not primitives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositional calculus core axioms and modus ponens
rubrics_metrics.description: Propositional calculus is taken as three axiom schemes: ϕ → (ψ → ϕ); (ϕ → (ψ → χ)) → ((ϕ → ψ) → (ϕ → χ)); (¬ϕ → ¬ψ) → (ψ → ϕ), together with the rule of modus ponens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tautologies can be checked by truth tables (decision procedure) which shows a proof exists but does not produce a Metamath derivation; finding short/elegant formal proofs may be challenging and often done manually in set.mm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate calculus rules used in Metamath (rule of generalization and equality axioms)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Metamath predicate calculus uses rule of generalization (if ϕ is axiom/theorem then ∀xϕ is a theorem) and includes axioms handling quantified implication, distinctness, existence, equality, and equality for predicates (axioms ax-4 through ax-9 and auxiliaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some textbook formulations include side-conditions like 'free for' that are awkward to implement; Metamath replaces them with distinct-variable provisos and auxiliary axioms (ax-10..ax-13) to obtain metalogical completeness suitable for mechanized proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: ZF(C) axioms overview and conservative choices in set.mm
rubrics_metrics.description: Set.mm adopts the standard Zermelo–Fraenkel axioms (Extensionality, Pairing, Power Set, Null Set, Union, Regularity, Infinity, Separation, Replacement, Choice) with commentary that some (Null Set, Pairing, Separation) can be derived and therefore are treated as derived rather than primitive in set.mm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Axiom of Choice is used when needed but proofs avoiding it are preferred when alternatives exist; set.mm sometimes includes stronger axioms (e.g., Tarski–Grothendieck) only when required for specialized areas like category theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use auxiliary axiom schemes to achieve metalogical completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Metamath extends Tarski's system with auxiliary axiom schemes so that theorem schemes expressible in simple metalogic can be proved using only direct substitution on axioms (no external metalogical notions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple metalogic consists of schemes with wff metavariables and/or set metavariables plus optional distinct-variable provisos; this choice simplifies automation and verification of theorem schemes within set.mm.
